study_type_evidence.quote: Balb/c mice were intranasally administered 5 mg/kg A1L35HR2m (n = 3) or A1L35HR2m-Chol (n = 3). Sera were collected from these mice before (0 h) and 2, 4, 8, 12, 24, 48, 72, 120, 168, 240 and 336 h after injection.
The ex vivo anti-SARS-CoV-2 D614G activity of A1L35HR2m or A1L35HR2m-Chol in plasma or tissue homogenate samples was detected as described previously.
The antiviral activities of the proteins were determined by using Caco-2 cells (10/well) infected by SARS-CoV-2 pseudovirus mixed with the inhibitors.

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: Balb/c, aged 6-8 weeks, from the Laboratory Animal Resources Center of Westlake University (safety and pharmacokinetics studies); sex not reported
in_vivo_species.quote: Balb/c mice (aged 6-8 weeks) for the safety and pharmacokinetics study were obtained from the Laboratory Animal Resources Center of Westlake University

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: Heterogeneous K18-hACE2 C57BL/6J transgenic, 6- to 10-week-old male and female (efficacy studies; individual experiments specify 6- to 8-week-old male mice)
in_vivo_species.quote: 6- to 10-week-old male and female K18-hACE2 were used for all in vivo efficacy experiments.

ex_vivo_detail: Plasma/serum and lung, nose and trachea homogenates were collected from intranasally dosed Balb/c mice, serially diluted, and assayed for inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 D614G pseudovirus infection. The dilution fold achieving 50% inhibition (DF-IC50) was used to back-estimate the peptide concentration in each sample, from which the half-lives and AUC were computed with PKSolver. Tissues were homogenized in 0.3 mL PBS and frozen. Live SARS-CoV-2 variants used in the study were isolated from respiratory tract specimens of COVID-19 patients in Hong Kong, but no patient was dosed.
in_vitro_detail: Pseudotyped virus inhibition assays in Caco-2 cells against SARS-CoV-2 D614G, Alpha, Beta, Delta, Omicron BA.1/XBB/BQ.1.1, SARS-CoV, MERS-CoV and VSV-G; SARS-CoV-2 D614G S-protein-mediated cell-cell fusion between 293T/EGFP/S effector cells and Caco-2 or Calu-3 target cells; biolayer interferometry against biotinylated HR1 on streptavidin biosensors; circular dichroism of peptide-HR1 complexes at 10 uM in phosphate buffer; CCK-8 cell viability in Caco-2 and Calu-3; microneutralization and RT-qPCR viral load reduction assays on VeroE6-TMPRSS2 cells with authentic Omicron BA.2.12.1, BA.5 and EG.5.1; dynamic light scattering showing A1L35HR2m-Chol micelles of 165 nm.

agents.name: A1L35HR2m-Chol (cholesterol-conjugated ACE2-HR2 fusion lipopeptide)
agents.sequence: not reported in the extracted body text; the body states only that A1 is an ACE2-derived peptide joined to the HR2-derived peptide HR2m through a (GGGGS)7 linker, with cholesterol attached at the C terminus via a bromoacetyl-PEG4-chol reaction with a terminal cysteine thiol. The residue-level sequences appear only inside the Figure 1A image and in the PEPLIFE2 metadata header, neither of which is a usable evidence source.
agents.sequence_source: RESULTS: 'we first introduced an ACE2-derived peptide A1 to the N terminus of the HR2m peptide through a relatively long flexible linker (GGGGS)7 to generate A1-(GGGGS)7-HR2m (A1L35HR2m)'; METHODS 'Preparation of A1L35HR2m-Chol protein'.
agents.chemical_identifier: Identity verified by LC-MS (Figure S3A); forms 165 nm micelles by dynamic light scattering; chemical structure shown in Figure 4A
agents.group_n: n = 3 for the pharmacokinetic and safety studies; n = 5 per group for the efficacy studies
agents.group_n_quote: Balb/c mice were intranasally administered 5 mg/kg A1L35HR2m (n = 3) or A1L35HR2m-Chol (n = 3).
agents.dose: 5 mg/kg for the pharmacokinetic study (5 and 20 mg/kg for the safety study); 2 mg/kg in the efficacy studies
agents.route: intranasal (pharmacokinetic and most efficacy dosing); intravenous in the Alpha-variant therapeutic arm
agents.dose_route_quote: A1L35HR2m-Chol (5 mg/kg, n = 3) or A1L35HR2m (5 mg/kg, n = 3) was administered intranasally to mice, and the plasma samples at each time point were diluted
agents.half_life_matrix: mouse plasma (also lung, nose and trachea homogenates)
agents.cmax: not reported as a concentration in the body; peak activity corresponded to a mean plasma dilution of 10,284-fold achieving 50% pseudovirus inhibition, with estimated concentrations plotted in Fig. 5B
agents.tmax: 8 h (plasma, lung, nose and trachea all peaked at 8 h post-administration)
agents.auc: 1,172 ug/mL*h (mean area under the concentration-time curve)
agents.pk_quote: The plasma t1/2 of A1L35HR2m-Chol was approximately 81.8 h, 30-fold longer than that of A1L35HR2m (t1/2 = 2.6 h) (Figure 5B; Table S1).
agents.notes_agent: Tissue half-lives: lung 89.8 h, nose 49.0 h, trachea 10.6 h. Peak tissue dilutions achieving 50% inhibition were 58,770-fold (lung), 18,231-fold (nose) and 1,959-fold (trachea), all at 8 h. Plasma concentration remained high even after 336 h.

agents.sequence: not reported in the extracted body text; described as A1-(GGGGS)7-HR2m, an ACE2-derived A1 peptide fused to the HR2-derived HR2m peptide through a (GGGGS)7 linker

concentration_time_figure.locator: Fig. 5B (plasma) and Fig. 5D (lung, nose, trachea homogenates); Fig. 5A and 5C show the underlying dilution-fold time courses
concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Estimated concentrations of functionally active peptides in the plasma (B) or tissue homogenate (D) samples.
concentration_time_figure.note: Concentration versus time after a single 5 mg/kg intranasal dose, with concentrations back-estimated from the dilution fold of each sample that achieved 50% SARS-CoV-2 D614G pseudovirus inhibition. Panels A and C plot that dilution fold (a %-activity-style measure) against time for the same samples.

bioanalytical_method: Indirect functional bioassay: serial dilution of mouse plasma or tissue homogenate followed by a SARS-CoV-2 D614G pseudovirus infection inhibition assay in Caco-2 cells, with the dilution fold achieving 50% inhibition (DF-IC50) converted to an estimated peptide concentration; pharmacokinetic parameters then computed with PKSolver software. No LC-MS/MS, ELISA or radiolabel assay is described.
bioanalytical_quote: The dilution fold of the serum achieving 50% inhibition (DF-IC50) was calculated. Based on the calculated DF-IC50 values, the concentration of peptides in the plasma or tissue homogenate samples was estimated
notes: Dosing for the PK study was intranasal, so an absorption phase exists, but the paper reports no absorption half-life and no absorption rate constant; half_life_absorption is therefore 'not reported' for all agents and nothing was converted. The half-lives were obtained by fitting estimated concentration-time data in PKSolver and no phase is named anywhere, so half_life_phase is 'unspecified' and half_life_elimination is left as not reported rather than inferred from an unnamed t1/2. A tmax of 8 h IS reported for A1L35HR2m-Chol in plasma, lung, nose and trachea ('The peptide concentration in the lung, nose, and trachea peaked at 8 h'), but no numeric Cmax is given in the body: the peak is expressed as a mean dilution fold (10,284-fold plasma, 58,770-fold lung, 18,231-fold nose, 1,959-fold trachea) with the estimated concentrations plotted only in Figures 5B and 5D. Tissue half-lives (lung 89.8 h, nose 49.0 h, trachea 10.6 h) are recorded in notes_agent alongside the headline plasma value of 81.8 h. Full amino-acid sequences appear only inside the Figure 1A image and in the PEPLIFE2 metadata header, so all sequence fields are recorded as not reported in body. The peptide concentration measurement is an indirect functional estimate rather than a direct analytical quantitation, which is a caveat on all reported concentrations and AUCs. Live SARS-CoV-2 isolates came from patient specimens, but no human was dosed, so the study is not classified as clinical. The virus challenge inocula (Omicron BA.5 and EG.5.1 at 10,000 PFU, SARS-CoV-2 Alpha at 200 PFU) are model-induction agents and are noted here rather than listed as agent objects.
